key_insight: Atomistic stiffness calculations coupled with EBSD-informed finite elements accurately reproduced the elastic response of polycrystalline NiAl under the study’s modeling assumptions.
engineering_relevance: The framework links crystal-scale stiffness and realistic grain structure to effective elastic properties for engineering analysis of NiAl components.
method: Calculate the single-crystal NiAl stiffness tensor atomistically.
Build a 3D polycrystal using EBSD-derived grain orientation and size distributions.
Simulate uniaxial tension with FEM and compare effective properties with analytical homogenization estimates.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports very good FEM–experiment agreement for Young’s modulus and Poisson’s ratio, with minor Young’s modulus deviations for the Hashin–Shtrikman upper bound and self-consistent approximation.
watch_item: No numerical errors are reported in the abstract, and accuracy depends on the atomistic inputs and reconstructed microstructure; no AI surrogate is described.
paper_title: Multiscale evaluation of the elastic response of polycrystalline NiAl using molecular statics, EBSD-based finite element and analytical homogenization methods
